rules.rule: Check for urgent suspected TB conditions
rules.problem: Type, trigger (possible TB) and coverage of the red box are right (vitals are routine and need no check). It inherits the Hemoptysis threshold and 'unaided' problems from its items. Because the trigger fires on any cough or fever (via the possible-TB rule), this 12-item check will run for every coughing or febrile adult.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible TB from TB symptoms, TB contact or abnormal screening CXR
rules.problem: 'Check for TB if any TB symptoms' as a possible TB diagnosis is reasonable. But the page's 'also test for TB even in the absence of symptoms' indications (TB contact, abnormal CAD CXR) are merged in as if they were grounds to suspect TB. The other two indications (DS-TB in last 2 years, PLHIV) are left out, so the treatment of that list is inconsistent. Cough alone and fever alone each make possible TB, which is very broad, though the page literally says 'any'.

rules.rule: Urgent: suspected TB with danger signs
rules.problem: (and suspected-TB (or red-box items)) matches the box heading 'Give urgent attention to the patient with suspected TB and any of'. Urgent is justified and the thresholds (RR >= 30, pulse > 120, temp > 39 °C) match. The only issue is the item-level imprecision (Hemoptysis volume, unaided walking).

summary: The most consequential problem is that the haemoptysis item drops the page's '>= 1 tablespoon of fresh blood' threshold, so any blood-streaked sputum in a suspected-TB patient is triaged Urgent. The possible-TB diagnosis rule also folds in the asymptomatic test indications (TB contact, abnormal CAD CXR) as grounds for 'suspected TB', and uses a generic Exposure+organism form where 'Exposure to tuberculosis' (event) exists. Otherwise the red box is faithfully and completely encoded with correct thresholds and Urgent priority; 'unable to walk unaided' and 'drenching' night sweats lose their qualifiers.
